# Influenza Prevention Clinical Compass
## Influenza Vaccine Insurance Authorization Guide

[Back to Assessment] (link: /influenzaprevention)

## Procedure Codes (CPT Codes)

### CPT 90686 (RVU 0.25)
Influenza virus vaccine, quadrivalent (IIV4), split virus, preservative free, 0.5 mL dosage, for intramuscular use
Device/Access: Intramuscular injection
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Vaccine product supply
- Administration of the vaccine
Note: For individuals 3 years of age and older. Specific vaccine brand may vary.

### CPT 90688 (RVU 0.25)
Influenza virus vaccine, quadrivalent (IIV4), split virus, 0.5 mL dosage, for intramuscular use
Device/Access: Intramuscular injection
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Vaccine product supply
- Administration of the vaccine
Note: For individuals 3 years of age and older. This code is often used for multi-dose vials or when preservative is not specified as free.

## ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes

- Z23 (Primary / Required): Encounter for immunization. Used for routine prophylactic immunization against influenza.

## Payer-Specific Authorization Requirements

Payer tabs: Medicare, Medicaid, Private Insurance.

### Medicare
Status badges: No Prior Auth (FFS) | Covered
Prior Auth Note: Influenza vaccines are generally covered by Medicare Part B without prior authorization when administered by an eligible provider.
Overview: Medicare Part B covers influenza virus vaccines. Beneficiaries are eligible for one influenza immunization per flu season. No deductible or copayment applies.

#### Coverage Criteria
Eligibility:
- Beneficiary is enrolled in Medicare Part B.
Frequency:
- One influenza immunization per flu season.

#### Required Documentation
Medical Record:
- Date of administration
- Vaccine type and dosage
- Route of administration
- Site of administration
- Manufacturer and lot number
- Expiration date
- Name and title of person administering vaccine

#### Submission Process
1. Submit claim with appropriate CPT code (e.g., 90686, 90688) and ICD-10 code Z23.
2. Ensure correct place of service and rendering provider information.

#### Common Denial Reasons
- Incorrect CPT or ICD-10 coding.
- Duplicate billing for the same flu season.
- Missing or incomplete documentation.

#### Known Payer Policies
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CMS | Covered | Annual influenza vaccine is a preventive service covered under Medicare Part B. |

#### Reimbursement Note
Medicare typically reimburses for the vaccine product and its administration. Payment is usually 100% of the Medicare-approved amount, with no patient cost-sharing.

#### Authorization Tips
- Verify patient eligibility and Medicare Part B enrollment prior to administration.
- Keep detailed records of vaccine administration.
- Stay updated on annual Medicare influenza vaccine policies.

### Medicaid
Status badges: No Prior Auth (FFS) | Covered
Prior Auth Note: Influenza vaccines are typically covered by Medicaid without prior authorization, especially for children and at-risk adults.
Overview: Medicaid programs generally cover influenza vaccines for eligible beneficiaries, often following ACIP recommendations. Coverage details may vary by state.

#### Coverage Criteria
Eligibility:
- Beneficiary is enrolled in state Medicaid program.
Age/Risk Factors:
- Coverage often aligns with ACIP recommendations for age groups and risk factors.

#### Required Documentation
Medical Record:
- Date of administration
- Vaccine type and dosage
- Route of administration
- Site of administration
- Manufacturer and lot number
- Expiration date
- Name and title of person administering vaccine
State-Specific:
- Any additional state-mandated documentation for vaccine administration.

#### Submission Process
1. Submit claim to state Medicaid program with appropriate CPT code (e.g., 90686, 90688) and ICD-10 code Z23.
2. Adhere to state-specific billing guidelines and deadlines.

#### Common Denial Reasons
- Patient not eligible for Medicaid on date of service.
- Incorrect or missing state-specific identifiers.
- Failure to follow state-specific vaccine administration guidelines.

#### Known Payer Policies
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| State Medicaid (e.g., California Medi-Cal) | Covered | Covers influenza vaccines for all eligible beneficiaries according to ACIP guidelines. |

#### Reimbursement Note
Medicaid reimbursement rates for influenza vaccines and administration vary by state. Providers should consult their state's Medicaid fee schedule.

#### Authorization Tips
- Familiarize yourself with your state's specific Medicaid policies for immunizations.
- Verify patient eligibility through the state Medicaid portal before administering the vaccine.

### Private Insurance
Status badges: No Prior Auth (FFS) | Covered (usually 100%)
Prior Auth Note: Most private insurance plans cover influenza vaccines as a preventive service without prior authorization, often with no cost-sharing.
Overview: Private health insurance plans typically cover influenza vaccinations as a preventive benefit, often at 100% with no copayment or deductible when received from an in-network provider.

#### Coverage Criteria
Plan Benefits:
- Coverage is subject to individual plan benefits and network participation.
Preventive Care:
- Generally covered as a preventive service as per ACA guidelines.

#### Required Documentation
Medical Record:
- Date of administration
- Vaccine type and dosage
- Route of administration
- Site of administration
- Manufacturer and lot number
- Expiration date
- Name and title of person administering vaccine
Claim Submission:
- Accurate patient demographic and insurance information.

#### Submission Process
1. Submit claim to the patient's private insurance company using appropriate CPT code (e.g., 90686, 90688) and ICD-10 code Z23.
2. Verify patient's insurance benefits prior to service to confirm coverage and cost-sharing.

#### Common Denial Reasons
- Out-of-network provider.
- Lack of medical necessity (rare for flu vaccine).
- Incorrect coding or missing patient insurance details.

#### Known Payer Policies
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blue Cross Blue Shield | Covered | Typically covers annual flu shots as a preventive service with no cost-sharing. |
| UnitedHealthcare | Covered | Generally covers flu vaccines at no cost to the member when administered by an in-network provider. |

#### Reimbursement Note
Reimbursement for private insurance plans varies. Many plans cover preventive vaccines at 100% of the allowed amount. Negotiated rates apply.

#### Authorization Tips
- Always verify insurance benefits and network status before administering the vaccine.
- Inform patients about potential out-of-pocket costs if they are out-of-network or if their plan has unusual coverage terms.
